A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same InnoEval work. All 51 pages in each version, including figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–H, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark comparisons in Tables 1–2, human evaluation and ablations in Figure 2, and further experimental analyses in Figures 3–5.

after.justification: v2 retains these original benchmark results, human evaluation, ablations, and supplementary analyses.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same extraction, iterative heterogeneous search, grounding, persona-based evaluation, and report-generation procedures. The appendix corrections do not establish an algorithm or model change.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the ICLR 2025 and NeurIPS 2025 idea datasets, point-wise/pair-wise/group-wise tasks, human evaluation, idea-refinement experiment, and Mamba case study. No evaluated domain or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains CoT, RAG, GraphEval, ResearchAgent, InternAgent, and ScholarEval. Comparator membership is also unchanged in Table 2 and Figure 3, including AutoSurvey in the search-module comparison.

E3.justification: Appendix E, Equation (14), revises the stated Topic Coverage metric from a union-based numerator to the intersection of idea topics with retrieved topics. Other evaluation settings are unchanged. The PDFs do not establish that experiments were rerun or scores recomputed.

E4.justification: The component ablations, backbone substitution, persona-count scaling, search and idea-refinement analyses, dimension correlations, and Appendix G case study retain the same tested questions and evidence. No supplementary experiment or analysis result is added or removed.

E5.justification: No repeated-run counts, seed information, uncertainty intervals, significance tests, or statistical estimation procedures are added or revised. Correlation and regression reporting remains unchanged.

E6.justification: Reported values and findings are unchanged, including InnoEval’s 74.56% ternary macro F1 and 22.09% exact group-ranking accuracy in Table 1. Table 2 and Figures 2–5 retain their results; the Equation (14) correction is not accompanied by revised Figure 3b scores.

T1.justification: Writing U for the union of retrieved topic sets, Equation (14) changes from |T_I ∪ U|/|T_I| to |T_I ∩ U|/|T_I|. This corrects the mathematical definition to bounded topic coverage for nonempty T_I. Other formal definitions and equations are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same methodological and dataset contributions, superiority claims across evaluation tasks, and claims of alignment with human judgments.

C2.justification: Interpretations of grounding, reviewer diversity, retrieval breadth, and evaluation dimensions are retained. Appendix A keeps the same discipline, modality, and efficiency limitations, and the Impact Statement retains the human-oversight qualification.

D1.justification: Implementation settings, data construction, baseline reproduction, persona construction, and resource-access information remain unchanged. Appendix H’s isolated symbol repair is typographical and does not establish a changed implementation setting.

R1.justification: Section 6 and the bibliography retain the same cited works and research positioning. Bibliographic entries reflow after the added acknowledgments without substantive citation changes.

P1.justification: v2 adds acknowledgments, replaces the preprint notice with ICML 2026 proceedings information, and adds Emine Yilmaz’s contact address. Appendix H corrects 'Precision ¿ breadth' to 'Precision > breadth'. Scientific prose and section organization remain essentially unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 4 is slightly enlarged without changing its plotted content. The introduction starts in the right column of page 1, and text and references reflow around the front-matter changes and acknowledgments. No figure or table is added or removed.

improvement.justification: The Equation (14) correction resolves a concrete inconsistency: v1’s formula cannot produce coverage below 1 for nonempty idea-topic sets, whereas v2 matches the stated overlap interpretation and Figure 3b’s bounded scores. Minor readability repairs also help. These are localized improvements; the method and empirical evidence remain unchanged, with no documented rerun.
